chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Every newborn is pledged with his Aqeeqa.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Aqeeqa for a newborn in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Aqeeqa as a recommended act (mustahabb) that secures the child's spiritual well-being and freedom from potential impediments. Scholars like Al-Hilli and Al-Majlisi interpret the 'pledge' (rahn) as a spiritual lien that is lifted through the sacrifice, ensuring the child's protection and the fulfillment of their divine rights.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa Al Sabaty, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Every new-born is a pledgee with his Aqeeqa’.
